qAndA.answer: The video does not specify the name of the star, only referring to it as the host star of WASP 76 b.
qAndA.question: What is the name of the star orbited by WASP 76 b?

qAndA.answer: The extreme temperatures on the dayside of WASP 76 b, reaching 2400 degrees Celsius, are hot enough to vaporize iron. This vaporized iron then condenses and falls as rain on the cooler nightside.
qAndA.question: What causes the iron rain on WASP 76 b?

qAndA.answer: WASP 76 b is tidally locked to its star, meaning that one side of the planet always faces the star (dayside), while the other side perpetually faces away (nightside). This results in a significant temperature difference between the two hemispheres.
qAndA.question: Why is the nightside of WASP 76 b cooler than the dayside?

Situated 600 light-years away, this planet offers a glimpse into extreme forces in the universe, where molten iron falls from the sky, transforming the air into a furnace. Explore the extreme conditions of Wasp 76 b, from scorching day-side temperatures to contrasting night-side climates.
